facts.raw_span: multiple (approximately 10) bluish, partially keratotic papules and nodules on the lower legs
The lesions had been growing very slowly in number and size since age 24
had been bleeding occasionally after trauma
right-sided hemiparesis and hemianopsia caused by an intracranial hemorrhage
recurrent seizures at age 4
lipolymphedema of the lower legs attributed to functional venous insufficiency with insufficient venous pump activity
had been wearing compression stockings for years
family history revealed similar conditions in the patient's father and aunt
father having died of an intracranial hemorrhage in his early 70s
Sonography: Demonstrated intradermal slow-flow vascular malformations with a maximum diameter of 1.2 cm

Biopsy revealed a well-circumscribed lesion with hyperkeratosis and acanthosis of the epidermis overlying a conglomerate of dilated venous-like malformations with continuous smooth muscle in the upper dermis, partly showing thrombosis
Detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant

The patient's presentation of multiple bluish, partially keratotic papules and nodules on the lower legs, and sonography and histopathology results, support this diagnosis.
The patient's presentation of lipolymphedema of the lower legs, attributed to functional venous insufficiency, supports this diagnosis.
The patient's history of recurrent seizures at age 4 supports this diagnosis.

rationales.F01: Multiple bluish, partially keratotic papules and nodules on the lower legs suggest cutaneous venous malformation and possibly cerebral cavernous malformation.
rationales.F04: Right-sided hemiparesis and hemianopsia caused by an intracranial hemorrhage suggest cerebral cavernous malformation.
rationales.F08: Family history of similar conditions suggests a possible genetic component, such as KRIT1-related cerebral cavernous malformation.
rationales.F09: Father's death from an intracranial hemorrhage suggests a possible familial component to cerebral cavernous malformation.
rationales.F12: Detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant strongly suggests KRIT1-related cerebral cavernous malformation.
